name: cheapglk
why: A minimal Glk library for running classic interactive fiction, a close call tied to the old-school text adventure world.

brief.what_it_is: CheapGlk is a C source library, version 1.0.7, that implements the Glk API, a standard interface for interactive fiction programs. The Glk spec page describes it as an extremely minimal Glk library that uses only stdio.h and allows only a single window, yet is fully Glk-compliant (Glk 0.7.6). A Glk program, such as a game or an interpreter, links against a Glk library to handle its windows, input and output, and the library supplies the machine-specific part. The page does not say more specifically what CheapGlk reads or writes beyond stdio.
brief.why_it_exists: Glk exists so that interactive fiction programs can run on many platforms through one interface standard, with a separate Glk library per machine. CheapGlk is the smallest of the listed implementations, aimed at a bare-bones stdio-only setup, while the page notes that RemGlk is 'not as cheap as CheapGlk' because it supports multiple windows.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives no mechanism for CheapGlk itself. It describes the general model: a Glk program calls the Glk API, and a Glk library implements that API for a given machine. The page's wider framing covers optional add-on layers (Dispatch, Blorb, Debug) that a library can include, but it does not say whether CheapGlk includes any of them.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not give build or install steps for CheapGlk. Its source is listed on the IF Archive under if-archive/programming/glk/implementations, which the page describes as the official archive of Glk libraries. The page does not say which compiler or build system CheapGlk expects, and the page does not describe a brew formula. The only dependency stated is stdio.h.
brief.standout: CheapGlk is deliberately tiny: a Glk library with one window and only the C standard I/O header, yet still compliant with the Glk spec. Its neighbours in the list (RemGlk, GlkTerm, XGlk) trade that minimalism for more windows or a specific display.
brief.status: The Glk spec page was 'Last updated June 2, 2025', and its What's New section mentions 2020 and later spec releases, so the parent project is maintained. The page lists CheapGlk at 1.0.7 with no release date, and the homepage gives no CheapGlk-specific commit or release date. Status for CheapGlk specifically: unknown, though the surrounding Glk project is active.
brief.caveats: The homepage is the Glk specification page, not a CheapGlk page, so the CheapGlk details here come from a single entry in its library list. CheapGlk allows only a single window, so it is not suited to programs that need several windows. The page says the list 'is not immune to falling out of date' and that the official archive is the IF Archive. The page does not state CheapGlk's licence. The homepage was reachable.
quotes: C source code for an extremely minimal Glk library; uses only stdio.h, and allows only a single window. Nonetheless, this is a fully Glk-compliant implementation.
The official and up-to-date archive of Glk libraries is on the IF Archive
